Nagykallo Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nagykálló, Hungary

Not demolished. Nagykálló's older Jewish cemetery, believed to have opened roughly 350-400 years ago, was in use from at least 1781 to a final burial in 1821 (see the Nagykálló New Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history). It holds the ohel of Rabbi Isaac Eizik Taub, founder of Hungarian Hasidism, whose self-composed epitaph reads: 'Here lies Rabbi Eizik, the rabbi of the holy village of Nagykálló.' Ruined, sunken tombstones surrounding his grave reflect his Sephardic heritage stylistically. The site remains an active and popular Jewish pilgrimage destination today.
